Montana's knowledge test appears to be administered via an examiner-controlled system at driver exam stations without these mechanics being publicly documented the way many other states publish them; also notable, the manual does confirm a driver license receipt is valid for one year and allows three attempts within that year to pass all required exams (this is documented and is reflected in the question bank), but item count/passing score/timing are left explicitly UNCONFIRMED rather than guessed, per instructions to never invent a shared or placeholder number. Content-depth rationale: this is an unusually rich and current manual (nearly 5,000 lines of extracted text) with concrete, quotable figures throughout -- exact GDL hour/age/passenger thresholds, precise equipment visibility distances (headlights, taillights, turn signals, reflectors, horn), BAC thresholds (0.08 adult / 0.02 under-21) and DUI penalty amounts, insurance minimums ($25,000/$50,000/$10,000) and misdemeanor fine ranges, parking-distance rules (fire hydrants, railroad crossings, crosswalks), following-distance and passing-distance rules (three-second/four-second/ten-second rules), roundabout and funeral-procession right-of-way rules unique to Montana, and a full illustrated warning-sign catalog. This comfortably supports a rich, non-repetitive, fully-grounded bank: 270 questions were written across 24 topic buckets (licensing/GDL, testing & documentation, vehicle equipment/lighting, safety belts & child restraints, traffic signs -- regulatory/warning/additional sign meanings, signals & pavement markings, railroad crossings, intersections & right-of-way, pedestrians & crosswalks, school buses & zones, speed limits/passing/turning, parking, sharing the road -- bicycles & animals, roundabouts & funeral processions, insurance, distracted driving & communicating, space cushion & following distance, adjusting speed for weather conditions, DUI/alcohol/drug law, health/fatigue/senior drivers, emergencies/crashes/enforcement stops, penalties & driving records, and basic driving mechanics/other services), each grounded in and cited to specific quoted manual text via source_note, with no invented facts and no reuse of the manual's own printed chapter-quiz questions verbatim (paraphrased into new distinct MCQ items instead).
